messages:
anna: heads-up — during the 09:10 ramp we saw a sharp spike in model-pull failures from our registry (mostly S3). x-requests failing with TCP resets and a few 502s. looks correlated with NAT gateway metrics in us-west-2.
infra-oncall-bot: alert: NAT_GW_PORTS_HIGH (natgw-usw2-a) — ports_used=63812, ports_total=65536
mike: confirmed from logs: repeated `connect reset by peer` when fetching model shards. example from model-agent logs:
```
2026-03-18T09:10:12Z model-agent ERROR fetch shard failed: dial tcp: connect: connection reset by peer
2026-03-18T09:10:12Z http retry attempt=3 url=https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/...
```
sara: quick check — can you run `ss -s` on a host in the affected subnet? curious about TIME_WAIT/SYN_RECV counts.
anna: ran it on one pod node, here's snippet:
```
$ ss -s
Total: 30000 (kernel 32000)
TCP:   28000 (estab 120, closed 27000, orphaned 0, timewait 26850)
```
anna: huge TIME_WAIT, almost all ephemeral ports consumed.
dan: oncall here — pulling traffic graphs. NAT gateway for AZ A is saturated, per-AZ SNAT port headroom near zero. starting mitigations now.
mike: immediate options: 1) add S3 VPC endpoint to avoid NAT for model pulls, 2) reduce concurrent fetches in model-agent, 3) provision an extra NAT gateway per-AZ, 4) implement per-node ENI egress (egress IP per node) so SNAT space is multiplied.
sara: low-effort fast mitigation — add VPC endpoint + throttle model-agent concurrency to preserve availability. long term: egress gateway / eBPF SNAT pooling to increase port reuse.
anna: I'm going to patch the model-agent configmap to drop parallel_downloads from 40 -> 8 in the next rollout. also opening PR to add S3 gateway endpoint for the affected subnets.
mike: command we used to verify S3 bypass worked: `curl -v --interface <node-eni-ip> https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/manifest.json` (should return 200 without going via natgw)
anna: applied configmap patch and triggered rollout (deploy-bot will post updates), reducing in-flight pulls per pod.
deploy-bot: deploy started: model-agent v2.14 -> v2.14.1 (concurrency cap)
dan: rolled in S3 gateway endpoint for the prod-egress subnets (us-west-2a, b). monitoring SNAT usage now.
anna: after both changes — SNAT port usage on natgw-usw2-a dropped from ~63k -> ~11k over 6 minutes. error rate for model-pulls dropped to baseline.
mike: verified by running a synthetic burst of 200 parallel fetches from a test node against S3 behind the endpoint and natgw:
```
# from test node behind endpoint
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/manifest.json >/dev/null & done; wait
ss -s | grep timewait
# timewait stayed < 200
```
sara: action items: 1) short-term: enable S3 VPC endpoints for all model-pull subnets (anna to finish PR), 2) add model-agent concurrency guard and jittered backoff (PR in review), 3) increase natgw per-AZ threshold only if needed (cost discussion), 4) instrument Console with SNAT headroom metric per-AZ.
mike: question on cost — adding per-AZ NAT gateways is ~$0.05/hr * n per AZ + data processing charges. can we quantify vs work saved by caching/endpoint?
anna: will run cost calc and post to #finance; initial estimate: extra natgw (3 AZs) ~$300/month + data transfer. pushing cache + endpoint is cheaper and reduces egress cost too.
dan: long-term: explore egress gateway (ingress-nginx-like for egress) or per-node SNAT using secondary ENIs so each node has 64k ports. also evaluate ENI-based source IP pooling via CNI features.
infra-oncall-bot: note: created incident ticket INC-2026-119 for NAT saturation and annotated runbooks.
anna: thanks team. keeping thread open for follow-ups. please add any missing items and tag me if you hit regressions. :thumbsup:
